Screening of the lamination window was initiated for the ASL-ASL target laminate and carried out at various conditions using the calender at the Department of Energy Battery Manufacturing Facility at ORNL. A stable lamination window for the ASL-ASL laminate was achieved ranging from room temperature (RT) through an intermediate temperature range (up to 210°C) and was followed by initial success for the lamination of the 3-layer, ASL-ASL-AFL stack. The key parameters for lamination of green tapes includes: gap height, line speed and temperature of the calender roller. While all three parameters are critical in determining the quality of the laminate, elevated temperature was found to be necessary for good interface quality in the laminate. Slurries of ASL and GDC have been formulated and successfully coated on a Mylar substrate. Figure 2 shows the coating of AFL and GDC layers onto the Mylar substrate via a pilot-scale slot-die coater (Frontier). The dried coatings showed identical color and morphologies to those received from Redox, which had been tape cast. Various coating speeds were screened to establish the relation of coating speed and thickness. Figure 3 shows the dry coating thickness of AFL and GDC versus coating speed while maintaining a pump speed of 50 RPM. Since the operation conditions are proprietary information for Redox, the numbers are removed from Figure 3. The dry electrodes are thin, down to the single digits of microns. While increasing coating speed renders thin coatings, it is critical to pay attention to the coating quality. In general, as a coating’s thickness is reduced thinner and thinner, defects may appear if the parameters fall outside the stable coating window for the particular slurry/ink. As shown in Figure 4, a homogeneous and defect-free coating is shown to be fabricated at a low coating speed. At intermediate coating speeds, minor edge line defects appeared at the edges of the slip. These defects are much more significant at higher coating speeds.
